title: Sebastian and the Crown
premise: Oscar Okafor, a runaway apprentice hiding under the name Sebastian, keeps ledgers for a guild that trades in impossible things — stolen years, borrowed faces, memories bottled like wine. When a dying courier presses a map into his hands, he discovers it charts the buried crown of the last true king, an artifact whose return would reignite a war the guild itself once ended by erasing it from every mind alive. Hunted by guild enforcers and royalist zealots alike, Oscar must decide whether justice lives in law, in memory, or in the courage to be someone new. In the end he destroys the map, gives the crown's location to no one, and chooses to keep his stolen name — becoming Sebastian fully — while smuggling the truth of what was erased into a single ledger page that outlives them all.
about_author: Orsen Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing disputed inheritances in coastal port towns. They write fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the people history forgets on purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. In the guildhouse of Vell & Sons, Oscar — passing as 'Sebastian' since fleeing his hedge-witch mistress — reconciles entries for traded memories and counterfeit years. He notices a page torn from the oldest ledger and covers for its absence. The beat: quiet dread; his false life feels safe precisely because it is small.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Weighing Door
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. A bloodied courier collapses against the guild's night door, pressing a wax-sealed map into Oscar's hands and gasping 'the crown remembers' before dying. Guild enforcers arrive minutes behind him. Oscar hides the map in a ledger binding and lies to his employer for the first time. Beat: terror braided with a thrill of agency.

chapters.title: What the Guild Erased
chapters.summary: POV Oscar, with interludes from the guildmaster Maren's private journal. Decoding the map, Oscar learns the guild ended the last war not by victory but by mass erasure — removing the true king and his crown from every living memory. His own apprenticeship suddenly looks less like escape than placement. Beat: vertigo as his identity as 'runaway' begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Zealot's Sermon
chapters.summary: POV alternating Oscar and Sister Ivet, a royalist preacher whose congregation dreams fragments of the erased king without knowing why. Ivet preaches restoration; her followers torture a guild clerk for the map's whereabouts. Oscar realizes both sides will burn the city to reach the crown. Beat: the comfortable neutrality of bookkeeping dies.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Salt Markets
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Enforcers corner him in the salt markets; he escapes only by using a hedge-trick his old mistress taught him — the first magic he's cast since running. A smuggler named Doss shelters him, demanding the map as payment. Oscar bargains for partnership instead. Beat: reluctant trust; the fugitive starts choosing allies rather than hiding places.

chapters.title: The Mistress Who Kept His Name
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Seeking answers, he returns to his hedge-witch mistress, Brannoc, who reveals she always knew where he fled — and that she trained him because erased bloodlines throw off 'gaps' she could feel. She offers to unmake the map's magic and warns it will cost his memories of her. Beat: grief foretold; love measured against duty.

chapters.title: Ivet's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Ivet, then Oscar. Ivet captures Doss and offers Oscar a trade: his friend's life for the map, promising a lawful trial and a restored kingdom where 'Sebastian' can exist legally. Oscar nearly accepts — the temptation of sanctioned identity — until he sees the trial records Ivet keeps: verdicts written before hearings. Beat: disillusionment with law as theater.

chapters.title: The Hollow Beneath the River
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Guided by the map, Oscar, Doss, and Brannoc descend into the flooded vault beneath the river and find the crown — and the erased king himself, alive, mindless, sustained by the guild's oldest working. He does not remember wanting anything. Beat: horror and pity; the artifact of justice is a man they must judge.

chapters.title: Crown of Ash
chapters.summary: POV all three principals converging. Enforcers and Ivet's zealots storm the vault; Maren arrives to renew the erasure, Brannoc to break it, Ivet to crown the king. In the chaos Oscar makes his choice: he shatters the crown's binding, freeing the king into ordinary mortality and destroying the map's power. Brannoc pays the price, forgetting him as foretold. Beat: climax — justice chosen over every faction's claim.

chapters.title: The Page That Outlives Us
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Months later, the nameless former king works the salt markets; Ivet's movement fractures without its relic; Maren negotiates a fragile truth-telling with the guild. Oscar, now answering only to Sebastian, writes one honest ledger page recording everything that was erased and seals it in the archive — unsigned, undated, waiting. Beat: bittersweet resolution; identity as something authored, not granted.
